analysis.title: US Pulse: FOMC tightening profile raised by 25bp to 4.50–4.75%
key_insights: ANZ adds a third 25bp hike to its FOMC forecast and now expects 25bp at each of the next three meetings, starting in December, taking the fed funds target range to 4.50–4.75% by March 2027.
ANZ cites signs of demand-pull inflation: October CPI confirmed a renewed acceleration in underlying inflation alongside robust domestic demand and early labour market tightening.

October three-month annualised core CPI rose to 3.75% and supercore CPI to 5.44%, per the ANZ narrative. Demand-sensitive components such as recreation, food away from home and personal services are firming.

Q3 private domestic demand grew 4.9% saar after 4.6% in Q2. The three-month average of nonfarm payrolls growth rose from 79k to 137k, and three-month annualised private average hourly earnings growth rose to 3.9% in October from 2.5% in July.
ANZ says the FOMC's October decision to hold increasingly looks like a policy mistake. A 50bp hike in December is not its base case but cannot be ruled out.
ANZ argues the FOMC should hike decisively at consecutive meetings despite Chair Warsh's preference for more than one set of data. If Warsh moves slower, larger increments may be needed later.

FOMC guidance has shifted from gradualism. Waller said a 50bp hike in December may be necessary, Williams said the Fed has work to do, Logan (voting) said two 25bp hikes are warranted and that the pace may need to quicken over winter, and Hammack (voting, a dissenter for a 25bp hike in October) favours small, frequent moves but would consider larger ones if behind the curve.
The October FOMC minutes are due this week. ANZ expects them to explain the hold and indicate the FOMC's sensitivity to AI-related fragilities in financial markets.

Housing is weak: existing home sales fell to a 16-year low, an annualised 3.75m, with mortgage rates above 7%. The October Senior Loan Officer Survey showed weaker demand across all residential real estate loan categories, and the NAHB index is expected at 23.0 after a near four-year low.
Week-ahead data: October retail sales expected +0.2% m/m headline, +0.3% ex autos and gas, control group +0.4% m/m. Industrial production is expected +0.1% m/m after +0.7% in September.

sector_views.rationale: Mortgage rates above 7% and affordability constraints are cutting buyer traffic. Existing home sales hit a 16-year low, builders are offering incentives and price cuts, and banks report weaker demand for residential real estate loans.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Three consecutive 25bp hikes starting in December. The path adds one hike to ANZ's prior forecast.
Not ANZ's base case, but cannot be ruled out. Waller flagged it as possibly necessary.

risk_factors: The FOMC may fall behind the curve if it tightens slowly, which could force larger hikes of 50bp or more.
Supply-side shocks continue to pose upside risks to inflation, per the Figure 2 caption.
AI-related fragilities in financial markets may affect the FOMC's sensitivity to tightening, per the minutes preview.
Housing is under pressure from mortgage rates above 7%, and weaker lending demand points to a drag on activity.

tension_points.bull_case: Fed officials such as Logan and Hammack favour moving swiftly and decisively. Waller said a 50bp hike in December may be needed to signal commitment to price stability, and ANZ expects three consecutive 25bp hikes starting in December.
tension_points.bear_case: Chair Warsh prefers to see more than one set of data before calibrating policy, which favours a slower pace. Slower tightening risks falling behind the curve and forcing larger hikes later.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Not stated as a level. The report points to the October FOMC minutes and further inflation and labour data as the evidence that decides the pace.
